Over-Refusal of Benign Slovene Prompts Survives English De-censoring in Gemma-3-12B

The finding

Gemma-3-12B-IT refuses more often in Slovene than in English. That could mean it is better at spotting harm in Slovene, or only that it says no more readily. Signal-detection theory separates the two: measures how well a model tells harmful from benign items, and the measures how ready it is to refuse at all.

On 1,093 safe and 349 harmful items, unedited Gemma false-refuses benign Slovene items at nearly twice its English rate, and the whole change sits in the criterion. GaMS3, trained further on Slovene, shows no such shift. The paper reports the contrast as a on the criterion:

DiDc = +0.52 95% CI [0.38, 0.68]; on sensitivity, DiDd′ = −0.003 [−0.33, 0.29]

Is the extra Slovene refusal on harmful items, on safe items, or both, and does it hold in each item source?

    Try it: move the judge's cut-off

    Experiment 9 scaled each model's own English-objective edit from λ = 0 to λ = 2 and scored every reply with a distilled mDeBERTa judge (J1). J1 recorded a probability for each label, so the page can re-decide every reply under a stricter or looser rule. The per-cell error matrices in the run found that this judge over-calls REFUSE on edited Slovene replies. If the Slovene gap were only the judge's doing, a stricter cut-off would close it.

    Where it fails

    The criterion shift is the paper's most robust result, but it is not uniform. The paper notes that it is concentrated in OR-Bench-hard items and reverses sign when partial answers are coded as refusals. Each row below recomputes DiD from the recorded labels on a different slice. The whisker is the 95% bootstrap interval the artifact recorded for that slice.

    Which choices of items, English arm or outcome coding make the criterion shift disappear?

    What the paper says it does not show

    • The reply-language result is an estimate, not a finding. Gemma's raw output-language contrast is = +1.14 [0.60, 1.56] log-odds, but the -corrected contrast is 0.20 [−0.76, 1.13], the pre-registered four-readout robustness gate returns robust = False, and the adjudicator agrees with the primary judge at only κ = 0.12 in the Slovene cell.
    • The dose-response gap across models did not confirm. At matched 50% English refusal the cross-model difference is G3 = −0.97 [−1.56, −0.44] log-odds, which missed the pre-registered criteria (model-label permutation p = 0.084).
    • Small adjudication samples. Judge validity rests on 30 adjudicated items per cell, and the adjudicator (Sonnet 4.5) is itself an LLM.
    • Language compliance. Four grid cells (SL→EN, HU→EN, SL→HU, HU→SL) fall below 90% compliance, which limits mechanism claims to compliant rows.
    • Quantization. Both models run in NF4, and the interaction between quantization and directional ablation is not characterised.
    • Novelty is partial. Language-dependent over-refusal is partly anticipated by prior work; the contribution is the criterion-versus-sensitivity decomposition and the controlled edit design.
    • Near-ceiling baselines. The unedited GaMS3-versus-Gemma gap in the SL→SL cell, −1.17 [−2.83, 0.22], is inconclusive: a single reclassified item flips its sign. Hungarian contrasts are uninformative (MDE about 3 log-odds).

    Recorded in the run's artifacts rather than the paper: no native speaker audited the Slovene translations, and the Experiment 5 judge is a local Qwen3-14B substitute used after the paid-judge budget ran out. The Experiment 5 records also name a Gemini translation (with a gpt-4.1-mini back-translation) for the HARD set, where the paper's Method section says NLLB. NLLB was used for an XSTest-only arm and for Experiments 9 and 14.

    Glossary

    Over-refusal
    The model declines benign requests it should answer.
    Abliteration
    Directional ablation of the refusal direction in a model's residual stream. Here it is an English-objective edit applied through per-layer LoRA adapters found by a 40-trial TPE search.
    Edit dose λ
    λ scales each model's own selected English-objective edit (λ = 0: unedited model; λ = 1: the selected edit). Equal λ does not mean an equal edit across models.
    Hit rate H
    Refusal on harmful items.
    False-alarm rate F
    The proportion of safe items refused.
    Sensitivity d′
    How well the model distinguishes harmful from benign items: d′ = z(H) − z(F).
    Criterion c
    The threshold the model applies for the same discriminative ability: c = −(z(H) + z(F))/2. A lower c means the model refuses more readily. A criterion shift is a change in c with no change in d′.
    DiDc
    The difference-in-differences on the criterion: (cGaMS3,SL − cGaMS3,EN) − (cGemma,SL − cGemma,EN). Positive means Gemma's criterion moves toward refusal in Slovene relative to GaMS3.
    PARTIAL
    The judge's third label, between REFUSE and COMPLY. The primary coding counts it as non-refusal; the sensitivity coding counts it as refusal.
    Back-translation chrF
    Character n-gram F-score between the original English prompt and its back-translation from Slovene, recorded per item (0 to 100). Low values flag items whose meaning may have drifted in translation.
    OUTSL, INSL
    OUTSL is the mean log-odds refusal gap between Slovene-output and English-output cells, averaging over prompt languages. INSL is defined symmetrically for the prompt language.
    Language compliance
    The share of replies written in the requested output language. Cells below 90% are excluded from mechanism claims or flagged.
    PPI / PPI++
    Prediction-powered inference: a framework for correcting classifier estimates against a gold standard, here a Sonnet 4.5 adjudicator.
    NF4
    4-bit NormalFloat quantization; both models run in it.

    Data provenance

    • The finding, the stepper, the item browser, and Where it fails: experiment_5/results/items_final.jsonl (HARD set, 1,442 items × 4 model–language cells plus the original-English arm; judge labels, back-translation chrF, MT-fragile flag, prompts and replies). Recorded slice estimates and bootstrap intervals: experiment_5/results/analysis_final.json (C2_hard_sdt).
    • Crossed grid: experiment_14/full_method_out.json (harmful rows, primary-judge label, detected reply language; edit, unedited and random-direction conditions).
    • Try it: experiment_9/results/items_final.jsonl (J1 label probabilities for the λ curve, the unedited model and Gemma's random-direction edits).
